title: Rob Davies reaches World Para Championships semi-finals as Grace Williams knocks out world No 2
seo_title: World Para Championships: Rob Davies into semi-finals
description: Rob Davies beat Kim Hakjin to reach the class 1 semi-finals in Pattaya, Grace Williams knocked out world No 2 Mingyu Zu and an injured Bly Twomey retired.
standfirst: The Welshman is one win from the final in his search for a first world title, while Williams came from a game down against the American and Twomey's knee gave way in her quarter-final.
body: Rob Davies is one win away from the final of the World Para Championships after beating South Korea's Kim Hakjin 3-1 in the men's class 1 quarter-finals in Pattaya on Tuesday, keeping alive his hopes of the one major title he has never won.

On the same day Grace Williams knocked out the world No 2, Mingyu Zu of the US, to reach the women's class 8 quarter-finals, but Bly Twomey's championships ended when her injured knee forced her to retire from her class 7 quarter-final.

Davies, 42, the Rio 2016 Paralympic champion and a five-time European champion, had a bye into the last eight. Kim, the Asian Para champion, had lost to him in five games at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, and Davies made the faster start, taking the first game 11-4.

Kim levelled by winning the second 11-9, but Davies took the third 11-7 and closed out the match 11-8 in the fourth. "It was really important to take that first set, because if you let him in and he gets a bit of confidence, you're in trouble then," Davies said. "I started quickly and that was my plan and luckily it came off."

He said he had prepared for the Korean players' long pimples in training. "I've been doing a lot of practice against these pimples ready for the Koreans so I'm very happy and it's been a good night," he said.

Before the championships Davies, who won silver at Paris 2024 and at the 2014 World Championships, said the world title was "the one I'd like now", as Eleven [reported when the squad was named](/news/gb-squad-world-para-table-tennis-championships-2026-pattaya-bayley-twomey.html). All the events in Thailand are straight knockouts, and his semi-final opponent on Wednesday is Chile's Vicente Leiva, the 24-year-old Para Pan American champion.
## Williams turns it round against Zu

Zu, who has won tournaments in Chile, Brazil, Taipei and Finland this year, took the first game 11-4. Williams won the second 11-7 from 8-3 up, then moved from 4-1 to 8-1 ahead in the third, prompting a timeout from the American, and took it 11-7.

Zu led 7-4 in the fourth, but Williams levelled at 7-7 and won it 11-9. "I used the first set as a warm-up set which isn't great when you're in a straight knockout, but I said to myself, 'forget about the first set, it's not the end of the match'," Williams said.

Williams, the world doubles champion with Fliss Pickard four years ago and a European silver medallist in 2023 and 2025, plays Chile's Florencia Perez, the world No 5, in the quarter-finals on Wednesday.

Twomey, 16, hurt her knee in a fall during the mixed doubles, in which she and Will Bayley [won bronze](/news/world-para-championships-2026-doubles-bronze-bayley-twomey-ryan-matthews.html). She beat Costa Rica's Kristel Morales Madriz 3-0 in the last 16 and won the first game of her quarter-final 11-7 against Hong Kong's Wong Yue Ching, the world No 5, but after losing the next two 11-4, 11-6 she could not go on.
"Going into the quarterfinals I didn't want to give away a medal, so I wanted to keep fighting," Twomey said. "Obviously, my knee is not the best and hopefully it is just a minor injury."

Chris Ryan, who had beaten Slovakia's Peter Lovas at last year's European Championships and again in Montenegro this year, won the first game of their men's class 2 quarter-final 11-6 and led 6-3 in the second, but Lovas won seven points in a row and went on to win 3-1. "It would have been a lot nicer to be going into the winter with a singles medal, but it wasn't to be today," Ryan said.

Tom Matthews beat Cyprus's Antreas Aravis 3-0 in the men's class 1 last 16, then lost 11-7, 14-12, 12-10 to Finland's world No 5 Timo Natunen, having come from behind to level the second and third games.

Wednesday brings Davies's semi-final against Leiva, Aaron McKibbin's class 8 semi-final against Italy's Ludovico Bini, Williams's quarter-final against Perez and Joshua Morizono's class 9 quarter-final against Ukraine's Lev Kats. The championships end on Thursday.
